Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT or THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL QOVERNPIENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II, EDSA cor. Mapagrnahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT 07 February 2006 VICE GOVERNOR RAMON G. MCBAIN 11 Provincial Capitol Building Iba, Zambales Dear Sir: mis refers to your request for this Department's legal opinion regarding the powers vested by law to an Acting Vice Governor during the official absence of the incumbent Vice Govemor, the latter being on official travel abroad. A perusal of your leffer also reveals your intent to inquire as to whether or not the Acting Vice Govemor can request for the realignment/transfer of funds from the offices of the Vice Govemor and Sangguniang Panlalawigan to the Office of the Govemor. In the meantime, your attachments disclose that in many instances, the Acting Vice Qovemor requested for a reversion of funds from either the offices of the Vice Govemor and the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for ure- appropriation" as: I. Intelligence fund of the Office of the Governor; 2. Indigency rund of the Office of the Governor; 3. "Donations" of the Office of the Vice Qovemor. Acting on the said requests of the Acting Vice Qovemor, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan enacted Resolutions authorizing the realignments and ordinances reverting certain funds and re-appropriating the same for other purposes. Hence, upon your return, the remaining fund of your office as of 23 December 2005 is P200.OO. Hence, your letter. In reply to your query as to the extent of authority enjoyed by an Acting Vice Govemor, please be informed at the outset that the Local Qovemment Code of 1991 (RA 7160), particularly Section 46 (a) thereof, does not explicitly provide for a nde of succession in case of temporary vacancy in the position of the Vice Governor. The Code only provides for the rule of succession for the same office in case of permanent vacancy therein, as found in Section 44 thereof.

-2- However, in the case of Menzon vs. Petilla (G.R. No. 90762, 20 May 1991), while the Supreme Court recognized the silence of the Local Govemment Code as to the mode of succession in case of temporary vacancy in the office of the Vice Governor, it nonetheless rule that, in order to obviate the dilemma resulting from an interregnum created by the temporary vacancy in the said office, the mode of succession provided for pennanent vacancy for the same office under Section 44 of the same Code should be made to apply. Hence, if a temporary vacancy occurs in the office of the Vice Govemor, such as for his travel abroad, the first highest ranking Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member, or in case of his inability, the second highest ranking sanggunian member, shall temporarily perform and discharge the functions of the Vice Governor in accordance with the rule set under Section 44 of the Local Qovemment Code. Therefore, an Acting Vice Governor is mandated to perform the duties and responsibilities of the office he/she is temporarily holding. May we note, however, that being an Acting Vice Govemor does not automatically vest upon the said official the power to preside over the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. In the case of Qamboa vs. Aguirre and Araneta (Q. R. No. 134213, 20 July 1999), the Supreme Court held that: "The creaäon of a temporary vacancy in the office of the govemor creates a corresponding temporary vacancy in the office of the vice govemor whenever the latter acts as governor by virtue of such temporary vacancy. This event constitutes an "inability" on the part of the regular presiding officer to preside during the sarwunian sessions which thus calls for the operation of the remedy set in Section 49 (b) of the Local Oovermnent Code conceming the election of a temporary presiding officer. The continuity of the acting govemor's (vice governor) powers as presiding officer of the sarwuniang panlalawigan is suspended as long as he is in such capacity". Verily, the above doctrinal pronouncement is applicable in situations where the Vice Governor's office is itself temporarily vacant. As regards the issue on realignment/transfer of funds undertaken by the Acting Vice Governor during your travel abroad, we noticed that aside from realignment, there was a reversion of funds, which are distinct from one another. Realignment/transfer of funds pertains to the authority of the Local Chief Executive or the Presiding Officer of the sanggunian, acting pursuant to an ordinance, to augrnent any item in the approved annual budget for: (I) their respective offices; and (2) from savings in other items within the same expense class of their respecåve appropriations (Sec. 336, Local Government Code). Ergo, for a realignment of funds to be valid, the following requisites must concur:

-3- 1. There must be an ordinance authorizing the Local Chief Executive or the Presiding Officer to augment any item; 2. The item to be augmented is limited to their respecüve offices; and 3. The funds from where the "augmentation" should come from should be the savings in the other items within the same expense class of each office(s respective appropriations. Note further that Section 336 of the Local Qovemment Code excluded the Vice Qovemor from being authorized to augment the funds in his own office (office of the vice governor). Reversion, on the other hand, refers to the power of the sanggunian to approve, upon the recommendation of the local chief executive, the reversion of funds no longer needed in connection with the activities funded by a continuing appropriations (Sec. 322, RA 7160). Meanwhile, what constitutes "funds no longer needed" is a matter that necessitates the exercise of sound judgment on the part of the local chief executive who recommends such reversion, which basically is not within the office of a legal opinion to resolve. Nonetheless, if the realignment or reversion made failed to comply with the provisions of the Local Qovemment Code earlier mentioned, judicial action/s may be availed of to rectify the wrong done or prevent recurrence of the same. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, TERES . CASTILLO Undersecretary legal:87/1.a cc: Director Rolando M. Acosta DILQ Region 11 Tuguegarao City
